[PATH:literature] Systematic literature review of participatory methods in indigenous community-based research, focusing on epistemic alignment and language revitalization — Synthesizes existing evidence across multiple contexts to assess whether the hypothesized relationship is consistently observed or contradicted in published studies.

[PATH:empirical] Comparative case studies of co-management boards in Canada (e.g., Haida Gwaii or Nunavut) that integrate Indigenous knowledge into land-use and cultural policy frameworks — These cases provide direct evidence of whether institutional frameworks actually integrate and elevate Indigenous knowledge systems through collaborative governance, and can reveal barriers or successes post-UNDRIP.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of literature on 'knowledge co-production' and 'Indigenous data sovereignty' in settler-colonial states (e.g., work by Kukutai & Taylor, or Smith's Decolonizing Methodologies) — This literature synthesizes theoretical and empirical findings on the power dynamics and outcomes of collaborative approaches, offering a basis to confirm or refute the hypothesis across multiple contexts.
